title: Instruction List: calling a function block and reading its outputs
summary: Call two instances of the same function block with CAL, pass their inputs by name, and read each output with LD Instance.Output.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish pump behaviour, start-up current or any real machine requirement, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Call a function block instance with CAL, passing its inputs by name, and read its output with LD Instance.Output.
See that two instances of the same function block keep separate memories.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: src/Latch.st declares the function block Latch with the inputs Set and Reset and the output Q, and src/PumpPair.il declares two instances, PumpA and PumpB. PumpA is already called: CAL PumpA(Set := StartA, Reset := StopA) runs it, LD PumpA.Q loads its output and ST RunA stores it. Write the same three lines for PumpB with StartB and StopB.
stages.checkpoint: Each pump starts on its own Start, stops on its own Stop, and one pump never moves the other.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: PumpA starts at {{t:10}} ms and PumpB at {{t:30}} ms. PumpA is stopped at {{t:50}} ms. Predict RunA and RunB at {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:70}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:PumpPair.RunA=true,PumpPair.RunB=true@30|Both ON}} at {{t:30}} ms; {{v:PumpPair.RunA=false,PumpPair.RunB=true@50|only RunB}} at {{t:50}} ms; {{v:PumpPair.RunA=false,PumpPair.RunB=false@70|both OFF}} at {{t:70}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starting program calls PumpA but never calls PumpB, so RunB never rises and stays OFF at {{t:30}} ms; add CAL PumpB(Set := StartB, Reset := StopB), then LD PumpB.Q and ST RunB.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named PumpPair and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:10}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:50}} ms: RunA holds after its button is released, RunB joins at {{t:30}} ms, and stopping A at {{t:50}} ms leaves B ON.
stages.checkpoint: RunA and RunB change at different times from the same block, which shows two memories. At {{t:90}} ms Start and Stop arrive together on pump A and it stays OFF.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: What would change if you gave PumpB the inputs of pump A? Try it and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: Each instance has its own copy of the variables of the block, so the same code serves any number of pumps; only the inputs you pass in CAL make them different. LD PumpB.Q before CAL PumpB would read the value of the previous scan. The scenario shows the logic only; it does not show start-up sequencing or a pump fault.

hints.text: CAL runs the instance with the inputs between brackets; the output is not returned by CAL, you read it afterwards with LD PumpB.Q.
CAL PumpB(Set := StartB, Reset := StopB), LD PumpB.Q, ST RunB, after the three lines of PumpA.

faultCases: The starting program calls PumpA but never calls PumpB, so RunB never rises and stays OFF at {{t:30}} ms; add CAL PumpB(Set := StartB, Reset := StopB), then LD PumpB.Q and ST RunB.
